reading.title: Our Holiday
reading.text: We had a wonderful holiday by the sea. The hotel was nice and the room had a lovely view of the beach. The weather was perfect: sunny and warm every day. The food in the restaurant was excellent, but the coffee was dreadful! On the third day we went to a market and bought some great gifts. On the last day the weather was bad and it rained, so we stayed at the hotel and played cards. My brother said, "This is a terrible day!" My mother said, "No, it is a lovely rest!" The journey home was long and the traffic was awful, but we were happy.

reading.title: Looking After My Brother
reading.text: Yesterday I looked after my little brother because my parents were out. I waited for him at the school gate. He was afraid of the big dog next door, so I held his hand. At home we listened to music and looked at old photographs. He asked for a glass of juice and I paid for his ice cream at the shop. He is good at drawing, and he drew a picture of our family. He is also interested in animals. Our mother thanked me for helping and said she was proud of both of us. Now I am looking forward to the weekend.

reading.title: Word Parts
reading.text: Many English words have small parts at the beginning. These parts are called prefixes. The prefix un- means not. For example, unhappy means not happy and unsafe means not safe. The prefix re- means again, so rewrite means write again. The prefix ex- is used for people from the past, such as an ex-wife. The prefix half- means fifty percent, so a half-hour lesson is thirty minutes long. Pre- means before, so pre-school children are too young to go to school. When we want to say something is not possible, we say it is impossible. Learning prefixes helps you understand new words easily.

listening.title: Prefix Examples
listening.script: An ex-wife is a woman who is now divorced. Something that cost ten pounds yesterday and costs five pounds today is half-price. A half-hour journey is thirty minutes. Informal clothes are jeans and trainers. It is impossible to read with your eyes closed. You must not smoke in a non-smoking restaurant. To redo something is to do it a second time. Unsafe means dangerous.

reading.title: A Day at the Beach
reading.text: It was a lovely sunny day, so we went to a sandy beach. The beach is popular with tourists because it is long and beautiful. My sister is a good swimmer. Her instructor says she swims very quickly. I am not a good swimmer, so I played in the sand. My brother brought a calculator to count how many shells he found. It was useless, because there were endless shells! In the afternoon we had a picnic. Our mother cooked on a small cooker. The food was delicious and we were full of happiness. We left the beach with a little sadness because the day was over.

reading.title: Mixed-Up Words
reading.text: English has many words that are easy to confuse. Last week I lost my keys and felt very upset. My brother lent me his spare key. I borrowed it for one day and gave it back in the evening. The same day I fell on the stairs because my trousers were too loose. Luckily I did not hurt myself. In the afternoon I went to the library, which is very quiet. I studied for my exams and I hope I pass. My teacher says my English is quite good. Tomorrow I will check my answers carefully, because I do not want to fail.

listening.script: Will you lend me your bicycle? Yes, take it. Thanks. Can I borrow your pen? Of course. The passport officer checked my passport. We use the mouse to control the computer. I hope I pass my exams. I have not studied, so I expect I will fail. In English the afternoon is from about twelve o'clock until five or six. The evening is from five or six until nine or ten. After that it is night.
